prerequisites: It is highly recommended to have the basic bibliography indicated for the course.
It is also recommended to have technical drawing material such as: square, set square, scale ruler, protractor and compass.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire the ability to generate all graphic documentation for a mechanical project.
Students will acquire the ability to model parts and assemblies in a parametric CAD.
Students will be able to make presentations of mechanical projects.
Students will be able to recognize and understand the representation of standardized elements.

assessment_methods.method: Submission of practical exercises performed in theory classes, practical classes and seminars
First partial exam (Theory exercises and content)
First partial exam (Tolerances exercises and content)
First partial exam (Parts exercises and content)
Second partial exam (Assemblies exercises and content)
Second partial exam (Drawing sheets: assembly drawing)
Second partial exam (Drawing sheets: exploded drawing)

assessment_rules: To pass the course via continuous assessment, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 must be obtained in Theory, Tolerances, Parts, and Assemblies, and 5 points out of 10 in Drawings; the final weighted grade must be 5 points out of 10 or higher. If the course is not passed by continuous assessment or if the minimum grade is not reached in any part, only the exercises corresponding to the unpassed parts will be taken in the ordinary call exam, requiring the same minimum grades. The grades for practical submissions and passed parts will be retained for the extraordinary call, where only unpassed parts can be retaken. Students who cannot participate in continuous assessment or take special calls (October, end of studies) will take a full exam accounting for 100% of the final grade, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 in Drawings.
